verdict.tagline: Endless roguelike variety hiding behind a punishing learning curve.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep item synergies and randomized runs
you master steep difficulty curves over time
not_for_you_if: you need clear in-game item descriptions
you struggle with strict directional controls
you want cloud saves that never wipe progress

distortion_flags.sentence: Positive sentiment increases sharply past the initial phase before leveling off among veteran players.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players struggle with rigid controls, technical launch hurdles, and hidden item mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game only allows shooting and attacking in four directions (left, right, up, and down).

citations.review_text:
Unfortunately this game is not for me but I can see the appeal.
The controls are one of the main reasons this game does not stick with me. Only having left, right , up and down as attack options feels too restrictive for me and paired with the main gameplay loop it just does not catch me. Add to that the barely explained mechanics and unfortunately it loses me entirely.
But on a positive note I really liked the artstyle although it is gross at times.

This game sucks. Devs think poop and farts are the coolest thing ever...

Keyboard only controls. Only shoot in 4 directions. None of the items describe what they do.
The aesthetics of the game around pain and suffering are simply not fun. The game itself (four way shooter) in minimally complex environments was not enough to pull me through.

Honestly the game makes a bunch of decisions that are just dumb. No item descriptions in game which is the dumbest decision for a roguelike game considering all the items we will pick up. None of the workshop mods that fix this are working for me and its wild that I would have to disable the achievements just to get this game to have the basic features of a roguelike. The controls are absolutely awful and clunky at best. Game forces full keyboard play which if I had known I wouldnt have purchased at all. Why do PC games feel the need to force you to use inferior controls? You are super floaty and dont stop right away after stopping. Overall this game is very niche and isnt just another roguelike given all the choices it decided to go with. I might keep the game and try again in the future but most likely it will sit forever in my library because there are much better roguelikes out there.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues with the game failing to launch or open properly after downloading DLC.

citations.review_text: Not working with dlc. Bad devs.
Game wont open after i downloaded the DLC. This game was running fine when i did not download it. I have tried all the fixes and the game still will not open.

I’m on Linux and Isaac is acting broken in a really confusing way.

I have Repentance, but in Steam the DLC does not even show up properly in the DLC section, so I can’t disable it from there. At the same time, the game seems to stop launching correctly because of it. Steam just tries to launch, then nothing useful happens / it gets stuck instead of opening the game normally.

From what I can tell, this looks like a Linux + native build / DLC detection problem, where Repentance isn’t being exposed correctly in the Steam DLC list and the game ends up in a broken launch state. It makes troubleshooting way harder because the DLC causing the problem isn’t even visible to manage normally.
it seams it also have same problem on MacOS until this get fixed my review is going to be this.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs poorly, citing technical issues such as controller disconnection requiring a game relaunch and audio glitches with buzzing sounds in one audio channel.

citations.review_text: Gameplay aside, this game runs really horribly. If your controller disconnects, you need to relaunch the game. You get audio glitches where a horrible buzzing sound runs through one channel until the BGM track changes. It's a shame, because if the developers spent more time fixing one actual release of the game instead of constantly re-re-releasing it under new names then they'd have a classic on their hands.

Massively overrated unless you're a tryhard. This game punishes you every step of the way if you do not play perfectly which is made overly difficult by some enemies that move rapidly and in unpredictible ways, rooms designed to make you suffer with terrible layouts and an item pool that's not only massive but has many actively bad items with no ability to even disable a few of them. You're also expected to know everything about the game and literally nothing is explained. I hope you like reading wikis or watching videos to learn most things about it...

If you're looking for a fun game that isn't overly difficult and gives you the feeling of constantly getting better and more powerful look elsewhere. If you're like me and can't tolerate BS enemies and rooms and also aren't super twitchy with insane reaction times then move along. There's much better and more fun titles out there.

Also ignoring the fact the game has severe technical problems with it's DLC. If you don't buy the complete version outright, instead going with the base game first then DLC later, expect to encounter issues "upgrading" to said DLCs if you choose to buy them. The DLC setup is also a complete fuster cluck. Utterly absurd...

TL;DR: Could be so much better but the game is designed to be frustrating and that's the point. I want to like it but it hates me and I can't abide that.

one of the best games ever the only downside is that i don't know what the power ups are but still peak game 10/10

Do you like RNG? If not skip this as your run is 90% based on what items drop or if a pill gives you a good or bad effect for the run. Items also have bar minimal description so any item that can't be summed up in 5 works, can't be figured out by using it, or if you just need more info you'll have to look it up outside the game. Even enemies are very rng (outside chasing you) they will have a set number of things they do. This is over say a game like megaman where most enemies and bosses have set patterns. The difference in this is that enemies are less predictable and have a higher chance of spamming moves (being cheap). The level design can be bad at times do to clutter and items being placed on islands you can't get yo (there should be a default jump or way to pull unobstructed items to you). On the plus side there are an insane amount of items, sidekicks, and weapons to find though not all of them are good and some can over right each other.

Overall the game is fun though a bit hard and not just do to boss/enemies can have unavoidable damage but also because some doors/items will damage you when you use them. Yes, You don't have to use them as none of them will block you from finishing the game if not used but you can paint yourself into a corner using them at the wrong time or the first time not knowing what it does. 
6/10

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Procedurally generated levels and unpredictable run elements drive the experience.

claims.claim: The game features procedurally generated levels and run variety where item combinations change gameplay.

citations.review_text:
For the most part, I really enjoy this game. It has roguelike elements, a distinct and memorable art style, incredible music, a million things to collect, and an addictive gameplay loop. 

BUT

Every run is based on *completely* random seeds. I've played plenty of games that incorporate RNG into their design. Inscryption, Hades, Blue Prince... All love their randomness. What makes this game annoying is how willing they are to allow that randomness to screw the player. 

Sometimes this means your items will be locked up, and the seed gives you no keys. Sometimes this means you'll get lots of money, but every "store" in the seed is a surprise miniboss. Every run, you have to re-discover what different pills do and about half of them harm you. I don't mind randomness, but nonstarter situations should be more guarded against.

The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is a rare example of a game that remains relevant years later thanks to its depth and thoughtfulness.
Each run is a unique set of challenges, where chance meets skill.
The item system is impressively diverse: combinations can completely change the way you play, turning a simple run into a strategic puzzle or a chaotic action game. Thanks to this, TBOI:R constantly surprises and maintains interest, even after experiencing hundreds of rooms and dozens of bosses.
The atmosphere is dark, but not repulsive, rather symbolic. The visual style and music create the feeling of a strange, unsettling world.
In conclusion, TBOI:R is a perfect example of how a roguelike can be simultaneously easy to learn and endlessly deep. If you enjoy roguelikes that combine difficulty, replayability, and deep mechanics, then this remains one of the best options.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features randomly generated runs where players can encounter situations such as stores being replaced by surprise minibosses or lacking keys for locked items.

Sometimes this means your items will be locked up, and the seed gives you no keys. Sometimes this means you'll get lots of money, but every "store" in the seed is a surprise miniboss. Every run, you have to re-discover what different pills do and about half of them harm you. I don't mind randomness, but nonstarter situations should be more guarded against.

[h1]Unpopular opinion time. Proceed at your own peril.[/h1]

The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth is a roguelite (having meta progression) twin stick shooter, that turns into bullet hell with later bosses. It has procedurally generated levels, and it has a simplistic, low resolution, intentionally ugly and gross art style.

Most importantly, it's a game that expects you play it and beat it, over and over and over and over again.

[h3]First problem: the game has hundreds of items and doesn't tell you what any of them do.[/h3]

In a well-designed roguelite, each item has a description of what the item does before you buy it or have commit to it. For example, in Balatro, you can come up with strategies and synergies from your very first run, because you can read the descriptions of what the different cards, modifiers, and jokers do, and begin to plan for what kind of setup you want to build towards. Same thing in Slay the Spire. Yet here you are expected to just waste all your coins, or your health/hearts, to blindly buy/pick items, that you have no idea if they will even be of any use to you.

[i]"Trial and error"[/i] as game design only works if you can reliably replicate your results. Playing this game normally, there is no reliable to way to test different combinations and synergies repeatedly (without putting in hundreds of hours or relying on a Wiki), as you are constantly at the mercy of RNG to even begin your "trial and error" experimentation. There's procedural generation of levels, and RNG items that change every time you play, and so, there is no strategy to this game before you have learned what the items do, through this [i]"trial and error"[/i]. 

So, when you first play the game, you are playing a lootbox simulator hoping that the item you pick up or spend your coins or life on, will help you. claims.claim: Reviewers note that online multiplayer suffers from lag due to its peer-to-peer connection instead of dedicated servers.

citations.review_text: Rightfully one of the most iconic rogue-like games. It's super fun, easy to run, and it has almost unlimited replayability. The game is also really easy to run, but your frames will begin to drop if you stack too many items on the same character (the sheer chaos makes up for it). If you ever get bored the steam workshop has an endless stream of mods you can add to spice up the gameplay. I wouldn't recommend getting the game for multiplayer, though, because multiplayer is very laggy.

an excellent and very in-depth roguelike with hundreds of hours of playability and a surprisingly sad and expansive story. 

before i played the binding of isaac, i had never touched any roguelikes and assumed i wouldn't like the genre at all. but upon trying it out (in the online multiplayer mode, a friend teaching me the ropes), i was blown out of the water by just how fun it is. seriously, this is one of the most fun video games i've ever played. the sheer amount of content in this game is bewildering and i love the progression system. defeat this boss 10 times, unlock this new thing which unlocks another boss, defeat that 5 times to unlock this and so on and so on. it's so fun to just hop in, try a new character and go for marks with them for unlocks. i love that every run is different; it just makes each run so special to me.

singleplayer aside, i'm so appreciative of the online multiplayer mode repentance+ offers.
the game works surprisingly well in multiplayer (as long as you're playing with the right people...) and it's such a fun time to just goof around with my best friends and get marks. i'm so thankful you're able to get achievements and marks in multiplayer, otherwise i wouldn't hold it this highly.
although, sometimes the lag is unbearable in online multiplayer. this is because it uses a peer-to-peer connection instead of dedicated servers. this decision seems completely unreasonable to me but i digress; hopefully one day it'll be switched.

all in all, if you're looking for a game to just sink your teeth into and have fun in, the binding of isaac: repentance+ is my top choice.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the early learning curve is unfun and the game is ruthlessly hard at the start.

citations.review_text: Very good game but it has a steep learning curve, and i did not know that if you get a deal after a moms heart fight you can continue the run without having to get it lives

This game just had me for like 6 years. 

- Kind of an unfun early learning curve, ngl. You'll really struggle in the beginning but your potential for growth is overwhelming.
- ABSURD replayability. The "hours on record" time for me is only since I officially bought it on Steam, before that a friend got me hooked on it playing at his place on Playstation and between these two I pirated it because I didn't have the funds to feed my addiction. I gotta be somewhere between 2k and 3k hours in this game and there is still stuff I haven't seen or done (Henry)
- Countless unlocks. If you hate that idea, just get a 100% save file. If you love progression, welcome home.
- Highly modable with tons of cool mods that give even MORE replayability to the game.
- Has been getting updates and patches for years.

I'd say it's a bit of an acquired taste with how ruthlessly hard it is when you first start playing. But once you see a clip of someone who knows what they're doing cleverly breaking the game - once that clicks for you? Game over, now you have to try all the billions of potential item combinations and creative ways to break the game for infinite money, health or damage or whatever RNJesus decides to grant you on that run.

I'm absurdly hesitant to give out 10/10s but I honestly could not name anything this game lacks or does in a suboptimal or annoying way. And with the most recent patches having made on-boarding for new players easier (you get item descriptions now! no more figuring out what the thing you just picked up does), even the steep learning curve shouldn't be that much of an issue anymore. 

So ... 10/10. Premium entertainment with the potential to last you so long that the per hour price is cheaper than breathing.
